chapter: The Jelly Roll Morton records and Minton's Playhouse
title: Rehearsing next door to Jelly Roll, Lips Page, and the Danish record
summary: Jelly lived at 131st Street next to where the group rehearsed; Caldwell also toured with Lips Page in 1945 and received a Danish record of the Morton album.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Okay, we were going to talk about how you came to make the record with Jelly Roll Morton in 1939.

Well, Jelly Roll lived at 207 West 131st Street, which I'm living at the same place now. And I was living at 2139 7th Avenue, which is on the corner of the next half a block from where Jelly lived, and at 209, next door to where Jelly was staying then, we used to do our rehearsing in there (unintelligible) bunch of us. And we'd go rehearse for these recordings.
Yeah, (unintelligible) used to rehearse there too.
Oh, did you play in Lippy's band?
Yeah, I'd play in Lippy's band.
We did a complicated Jazz concert in 1945, that spring, we toured. Yeah, we toured with them.
All right, after that -- I missed that.

Yeah, uh-huh, and that's when Jelly his last instrumental wrote these tunes and this was a dance recording, in 1939. When I was in Denmark last year for the jazz concert, This fellow's got a music store and got a fine band, and I was invited to his house for dinner and all, and he gave me a small recording which was taken off the master records of the album we made with Jelly. And it was four numbers, two on each side, and I said, well, I appreciate it. He said, well, Happy, after you (unintelligible), I got something to give you, and he presented me with it. I got it home now.

So I had taken the -- all the records I'd made with Mezzrow Jelly and Bence Roet, Eddie Condon, Jack Bland, Red Allen, and I put them on one album. See, I recorded them all and put them on all one album. So I don't know whether you have all of them or not, but I'll give you the album.
